thread:
Ravi K: quick sync after the active/active workshop. we still need a clear policy for consent-sensitive tenants when routing and failover cross regions. options on table: strict-residency-only (reject non-resident writes), tiered-consent (resident approval or shadow-apply), and graceful-degrade (accept then audit). thoughts?
Nina P: we should avoid surprise behavior for enterprise customers. strict-residency-only by default for tenants with legal annotations, but allow tiering for others. default policy should be visible in tenant settings and contract.
Diego M: technically strict-residency-only is easiest to reason about, but it's brittle under network partitions. for availability, tiered-consent with explicit transfer seems safer: client attempts local write -> server returns 409 with transfer token -> transfer proceeds. that's predictable.
Ellen H: operators reminded that transfer-heavy tenants will cause a lot of cross-region traffic. we need quota and throttles per-tenant. propose: transfer_quota per minute and a backoff that escalates to quarantine. Also emit transfer_rate_exceeded metric.
Ravi K: agreed on throttles. another nuance: what if client SDKs don't implement the 409 flow? we could do server-first fallback: try client-hint X-Region first, otherwise initiate a server-side transfer synchronously up to a short timeout, then fail. but that adds latency to every uncached write.
Nina P: can we detect SDK capabilities from user-agent or provisioning metadata? then we can choose hint-first for modern SDKs and server-transfer for legacy ones. store sdk_capability in tenant metadata.
Diego M: good idea. For active-active session affinity, we also need a canonicalization step for tenant's residency_policy so proxies can short-circuit routing. add header X-Residence-Policy: strict|tiered|grace.
Ellen H: monitoring: add counters for attempts, transfers, transfer_failures, transfer_latency_p95, and quarantine_count. SLO proposal: successful resident writes 99.9% within 300ms for strict and 95% within 2s for tiered under normal load.
Ravi K: legal asked for auditable events for any non-resident write: resident_approval_event with who/when and evidence. make handoff tokens signed and short-lived so audit trail includes proof.
Nina P: agree on signed tokens. also support an admin override flow for customer-support with an audit log entry. require 2FA for overrides.
Diego M: edge-case: simultaneous write bursts across regions causing two competing transfers. proposal: transfer must be serialized at resident controller using compare-and-swap on lease key. if conflict, return conflict metric and produce audit entry.
Ellen H: operator flow for quarantine: auto-quarantine when transfer failure rate > 10% for 5m and transfer_count > 50 in same window. when quarantined, we flip tenant to read-only and require manual review. console shows a prominent banner and an auto-created incident channel.
Ravi K: owners and action items: Nina -> tenant metadata key sdk_capability + residency_policy UI (owner: Nina). Diego -> implement signed handoff token + resident transfer API (owner: Diego). Ellen -> alerts + quota circuit-breaker + Grafana panels (owner: Ellen). Ravi -> write updated policy section into RFC-239 follow-up and sequence diagrams (owner: Ravi). Ops-bot: create tasks with labels rfc-239, multi-region, residency-policy.
Nina P: I'll also add an API to let tenants opt into "best-effort-availability" which enables tiered-consent for non-legal routes. must be explicit at provisioning.
Diego M: prototype note: start with controlled canary: 5% of tenants with low risk flag, enable tiered-consent, collect metrics for 2wks. toggles: ENABLE_TIERED_CONSENT, TRANSFER_QUOTA=20/min, TOKEN_TTL=30s.
Ellen H: will add quarantine runbook and a deref checklist for CS and Legal. also add metric dashboards for per-tenant transfer bandwidth so we can charge if needed later.
Ravi K: good. leaving thread for any last concerns. tag @Diego and @Ellen for sync. :thumbsup:
